derivation.public_item_instrument: syn parse of the crate source, walking public type aliases, structs, enums, enum variants, inherent public associated functions and trait impls. Each row records a normalized shape covering derives, field names and types, and signatures, so a field or derive change cannot land under an unmoved row. Type rendering is total over the shapes these sources use and fails closed on anything else rather than approximating.
derivation.consumer_instrument: Whole-word scan for perl_ast_v2, perl-ast-v2, ast_v2 and perl_ast::v2 across .rs and .toml files under the gating scan roots, plus a pattern for perl_parser_core's unqualified DiagnosticId / MissingKind re-export, which names none of those tokens. Word boundaries are required on both sides, so ast_v2 does not match ast_v2_lifecycle_audit. The scan finds references and, separately, whether a reference occurs in code or only in a comment: the role column is authored, but a file that reaches the package from code cannot be given a non-gating role.
derivation.non_gating_note: policy_inventory, docs_reference and release_metadata rows are recorded evidence and are deliberately not part of the gating denominator: a prose mention or a crate-name string is not production use. They are still checked — inside the scan roots a non-gating row must still be found by the scan, and outside them the file must exist — so a stale row cannot survive either way.

public_items.derived_shape: struct Node derives[Clone, Debug, PartialEq] { id: NodeId, kind: NodeKind, range: Range }
public_items.parity_note: The production AST also has a Node struct, but the contracts differ: production is { kind, location: SourceLocation }, v2 is { id: NodeId, kind: NodeKind, range: Range }. The Range carries byte/line/column positions, which is a representation of position and not a proved incremental contract — nothing here binds a node to a source revision or maps it across an edit, so the incremental-parsing claim in the crate docs is unproven at this layer.

public_items.derived_shape: fn new(id: NodeId, kind: NodeKind, range: Range) -> Self
public_items.parity_note: Infallible constructor taking a caller-supplied id and range. It validates neither, so node identity uniqueness and range ordering are caller obligations rather than type invariants.

ruling.rationale: The package is a real published surface but does not earn an independent lifecycle. Against the five retain clauses: there is no separate semver or release cadence (ev:coordinated-release); there are no external consumers who should avoid the larger canonical package (ev:reverse-dependencies observes only first-party dependents); there is no public proposition owned only by perl-ast-v2, because every public item is already reachable through perl_ast::v2 and two of them are additionally public API of perl-parser-core; and the compatibility shell can satisfy the lifecycle precisely because the canonical path already exists and is the documented one. The unique experimental propositions the package does hold — NodeId identity, DiagnosticId/ErrorRef lightweight recovery, granular MissingKind, and the depth-limited debug projection — justify keeping a distinct v2 namespace with an explicit contract. They do not justify a second package identity, because a namespace under the canonical package preserves all of them. Absorb here means moving the implementation under perl_ast::v2 and leaving perl-ast-v2 as a forwarding package; it does not mean merging v1 and v2 semantics, and it does not authorize deleting the published package.
ruling.compatibility_window: The forwarding perl-ast-v2 package is retained until #8847 can show, on evidence current at that time, that no third-party reverse dependency exists on any published version and that at least one further coordinated release has shipped with the forwarding shell in place. Deletion before that window closes is not authorized by this ruling. The four downstream re-export paths (rx:parser-core-engine, rx:parser-core-root, rx:parser, rx:parser-compat) are owned by their own crates and are out of this window's scope.
ruling.reversal_condition: Move the ruling to `retain` only on concrete evidence of an independent contract: a third-party reverse dependency on crates.io, a release cadence that diverges from the workspace version, or a public proposition that exists only under the perl_ast_v2 path and cannot be served by perl_ast::v2. Package existence, publish allowlisting, docs.rs metadata and experimental branding are explicitly below this threshold, and the loader enforces that a retain ruling must name independent-lifecycle evidence.
unknowns: Non-registry external use (vendored copies, private forks) is not observable with any instrument available here; ev:external-source-search records this as unavailable rather than as zero.

limitations: The consumer scan is textual. The first revision of this inventory recorded the unqualified perl_parser_core::DiagnosticId / MissingKind re-export as a blind spot and then wrongly asserted no consumer used it; crates/perl-parser-core/tests/diagnostic_id_tests.rs did, and was missing. That path is now matched directly by the loader, in both its qualified and grouped-import forms, so it is checked rather than assumed. The residual gap is narrower but real: a consumer reaching the package through a grouped import such as use perl_ast::{v2, ast}, through a wildcard use perl_parser_core::*, or through a locally aliased re-export of its own, still names no matched token. No such consumer exists on the authored basis, and the instrument cannot promise it.
syn sees declarations, not semantics. The public-item denominator is exact; whether a consumer depends on a variant's meaning rather than its name is an authored judgement.

Per-variant consumer attribution was resolved by alias-aware analysis of each consumer file, because v1 and v2 share 16 variant names. That analysis is authored input to this manifest, not a check the loader re-runs; the loader verifies that every consumer id resolves and that every named production counterpart still exists.
External evidence is a point-in-time registry observation from 2026-09-05. It ages, and the loader cannot refresh it.
This audit does not claim v2 is parity-complete, does not move source, does not change AST semantics, and does not authorize removing the published package.

The `equivalent` relation is asserted at field level only — same field names, same field types, and no child Node through which the differing node contract could leak. It never claims the two enclosing Node contracts are interchangeable.
